explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/477: is there an integer polynomial f of degree ≥ 2 and A ⊆ ℤ such that every n is uniquely a + b with a ∈ A and b ∈ f(ℤ)? Solved yes: GPT constructions work for f(n) = n^d, d ≥ 6 even. The statement asserts ∃ f with 2 ≤ degree and A such that every z has a unique pair in A × range(f) summing to z. Uniqueness of pairs (a, b) matches 'exactly one a and b'. Faithful.
